scope.description: Local retained-history representation after one failing conflict-reconciliation invocation. Begin with consistent retained logs and cached metadata, successfully delete an uncommitted conflicting suffix, fail replacement storage without writing replacement entries, and compare getLastEntry against independently inspected retained storage and snapshot metadata immediately after handler return.
assumptions: Initial cached last-log identity agrees with the actual LogStore.
The deleted suffix is above both the committed index and the retained snapshot index.
DeleteRange succeeds and removes the requested inclusive range.
The controlled StoreLogs failure writes no replacement entries; this is an explicit interface fault scenario, not an observed built-in adapter behavior.
No concurrent snapshot publication or other history mutation occurs during the comparison.
excluded: Proof that a selected production adapter realizes this failure sequence
Proof of a legal cluster history producing a later request with the deleted predecessor identity
Incorrect quorum commitment, application, or client completion

properties.reason: Actual result fields are compared after independent prerequisite association

adaptations: Construct a bounded follower fixture directly instead of starting cluster background workers; initialize consistent cached and stored history.
Use an interface fault adapter whose replacement StoreLogs returns an error without writes; this does not establish exposure in any production adapter.
Use a transport adapter implementing only the peer encoding and decoding methods reached by this invocation; no network delivery or scheduling is modeled.
Emit observations around actual calls without modifying the handler or state accessor.
boundaries: Proof that a selected production adapter realizes this failure sequence
Proof of a legal cluster history producing a later request with the deleted predecessor identity
Incorrect quorum commitment, application, or client completion
The fault adapter establishes an explicit interface scenario, not a production storage failure reproduction.
Direct fixture initialization does not establish a complete legal cluster history or network schedule.
The concrete case has no retained snapshot; concurrent snapshot changes and partial replacement writes remain outside this experiment.
The comparison does not establish a later request consuming stale metadata, subsequent success, incorrect commitment, application, or client completion.
The executed case uses direct fixture initialization and an injected interface fault; it does not establish a production adapter failure or a complete reachable cluster history.

The supplied trace supports only the local mismatch at handler return. Subsequent predecessor consumption, successful AppendEntries, quorum commitment, application, and client consequences remain unresolved.
The execution has no retained snapshot, no concurrent history mutation, and no partial replacement writes; it does not exercise those variants.

Supporting InmemStore and snapshot-store implementations are cited by the plan but are not attached here. This review relies on their documented interface roles, the supplied harness calls, and the actual correlated observations; it does not independently audit those implementations.
No named semantic issue was supplied for resolution, and this review does not itself change the machine assessment's confirmation fields.
